title: Solid figures at the market

pedagogy.rationale: Learners handle real objects first, then name faces, edges and vertices; the 3D lab (when released) only augments the real objects.

prerequisiteAssumptions: Learners can name flat shapes: square, rectangle, circle, triangle.

misconceptions.description: Counts only the faces they can see in a picture, saying a cube has 3 faces.
misconceptions.response: Turn a real box or die over: the hidden faces still count. A cube has 6 faces.
An edge is a line where two faces meet; a vertex is a corner where edges meet.

scenes.title: Shapes at Waterside Market
scenes.learnerAction: Name one object at home with the same shape as a market object.

content.body:
At Waterside Market you can see a football, a tin of tomato paste, a box of soap and an ice cream cone. They are not flat: they are **solid figures**.

What makes a ball different from a box?

accessibility.textAlternative: Market objects are solid figures: a football, a tin, a soap box and an ice cream cone. How is a ball different from a box?

scenes.title: What you will be able to do

content.body: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
keyPoints: Identify spheres, cylinders, cones, cubes and rectangular prisms.
Count the faces, edges and vertices of a solid, including the hidden ones.

accessibility.textAlternative: Goal: identify five solid figures and count their faces, edges and vertices.

scenes.title: Faces, edges and vertices
scenes.learnerAction: Hold a box and touch a face, an edge and a vertex as you read.

content.body:
A **face** is a flat or curved surface. An **edge** is where two faces meet. A **vertex** is a corner where edges meet.

A sphere (a ball) has one curved face and no edges or vertices. A cube (a die) has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

accessibility.textAlternative: A face is a surface, an edge is where two faces meet, a vertex is a corner. A sphere has no edges or vertices; a cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

offline.note: Real objects are the core modality.

scenes.title: Meet the five solids
scenes.learnerAction: Open each solid and find a real object like it.

content.body: Open each solid. Find an object in the classroom or at home with the same shape.

steps.label: Sphere
steps.description: Like a football: one curved face, no edges, no vertices.

steps.label: Cylinder
steps.description: Like a closed tin: 2 flat circle faces, 1 curved face, 2 curved edges, no vertices.

steps.label: Cone
steps.description: Like a paper hat: 1 flat circle face, 1 curved face, 1 edge, 1 vertex at the point.

steps.label: Cube
steps.description: Like a die: 6 equal square faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices.

steps.label: Rectangular prism
steps.description: Like a soap box: 6 rectangle faces in 3 matching pairs, 12 edges, 8 vertices.

hints: Turn the real object over to find hidden faces.

accessibility.textAlternative: Sphere: no edges or vertices. Cylinder: 2 flat and 1 curved face. Cone: 1 vertex. Cube: 6 equal squares, 12 edges, 8 vertices. Rectangular prism: 6 rectangles, 12 edges, 8 vertices.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Each solid is a button; press Enter to open it.

offline.note: Text with real objects; no device needed.

scenes.title: Explore the solids in 3D
scenes.learnerAction: Turn each solid and tap the cube's vertices.

content.body: In the solids lab, turn each solid to see its hidden faces. Find the solid with no flat faces, then tap all 8 vertices of the cube.

fallback.content: Use real objects instead: a ball, a closed tin, a paper cone hat, a die and a box. Turn each one over and record its faces, edges and vertices in a table in your book.

scenes.expectedObservation: Learners select the sphere as the solid with no flat faces and find all 8 vertices of the cube.

accessibility.textAlternative: In the lab or with real objects: the sphere has no flat faces, and a cube has 8 vertices, including ones hidden at the back.
accessibility.keyboardPath: The lab has a button for every action; the paper table works with no device.

offline.note: The lab adds 3D turning; the real-object table is the core modality.

scenes.title: Quick check
scenes.learnerAction: Choose an answer for each question.

content.body: Choose an answer for each question.

items.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?

options.feedback: Those are the faces you can see at once. Turn it over: the hidden faces count too.
Yes. Top, bottom, front, back, left and right: 6 faces.
8 is the number of vertices (corners), not faces.
12 is the number of edges, not faces.

items.prompt: A closed tin of tomato paste is shaped like which solid?

options.feedback: A cone has one point (vertex). A tin has two flat circle ends.
Yes. Two flat circle faces joined by a curved face.
A sphere has no flat faces. A tin has two.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two questions: how many faces a cube has, and which solid a closed tin is.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space.

scenes.title: What did turning the object show you?

content.body: Write a short answer in your own words.

prompts.prompt: Why can a picture of a box make you count the wrong number of faces?

accessibility.textAlternative: Write why a picture of a box can make you miss some faces.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to the text box and type.

content.body: Answer each question. Your answers are checked by the school's learning system, not on this device.

accessibility.textAlternative: Final questions naming solids and counting their faces, edges and vertices.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space.

offline.note: Answers wait on the device and are scored after reconnecting.

fallback.content: Your teacher shows real objects and records your answers on paper.

labProposals.rationale: Turning solids in 3D shows hidden faces and vertices; the lab augments, never replaces, handling real objects.
